items.newsletter: Review & Preview — September Blues / Barron's Daily — 2 Shining Lights in Bonds Gloom
items.headline: U.S.-Iran strikes intensify around Hormuz, sending Brent and global yields sharply higher
items.category: Geopolitics / Energy / Macro / Rates / Capital Allocation
items.summary: Reuters reports the heaviest U.S.-Iran exchange since July, including strikes near Hormuz, Iranian retaliation against U.S. bases and damage to tankers. Brent traded above USD 95 intraday while the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield moved toward 4.82%, extending the global bond rout.
items.whyItMatters: The energy shock and rate shock are now reinforcing each other. AGCI lowers broad equity risk appetite, keeps staggered duration and a moderate energy hedge, and waits for evidence that shipping and inflation risk are stabilizing before deploying more beta.
items.agciSignal: HORMUZ ESCALATION / OIL-INFLATION-RATES FEEDBACK / PRICE DISCIPLINE

items.headline: AGCI Greed falls 16 points to 71 while valuation stays extreme at 85; regime shifts to Correction
items.summary: The live AGCI engine now reads Greed 71/100, down 16 points in one day, while Valuation remains 85/100. The regime changed from Mid Bull to Correction and the matrix signal changed from EUPHORIA_RISK to PRICE_DISCIPLINE.
items.whyItMatters: Sentiment is finally cooling, but valuation has not reset. AGCI treats the correction as improved optionality rather than a blanket buy signal: liquidity remains valuable and new purchases should be staged only inside fair value with margin of safety.
items.agciSignal: CORRECTION / GREED RESET WITHOUT VALUATION RESET / WAIT FOR PRICE

items.newsletter: Barron's Daily — 2 Shining Lights in Bonds Gloom / 2 Sep 2026
items.headline: Micron and Broadcom become the next AI quality tests as bond yields pressure long-duration technology
items.summary: Barron's flags Micron as a current catalyst and Broadcom as a key earnings test for the AI trade while the broader market absorbs higher bond yields. The setup shifts attention from AI demand alone toward pricing power, contracted demand, margins and resilience to a higher discount rate.
items.whyItMatters: AGCI keeps AI exposure selective. Memory and custom-silicon leaders can remain structurally strong, but the cost of capital now matters more; position sizing should distinguish funded demand and cash-flow conversion from narrative-driven backlog.
items.agciSignal: AI QUALITY TEST / PRICING POWER + FUNDED DEMAND / HIGHER DISCOUNT RATE

items.headline: Chevron commits USD 7 billion to double Venezuela output over five years
items.summary: Chevron announced a roughly USD 7 billion plan to expand Venezuelan crude production from about 290,000 barrels per day toward 600,000 bpd over five years under a revised operating framework.
items.whyItMatters: Venezuela can become a medium-term counterweight to Middle East supply risk, but it does not solve the near-term Hormuz shock. AGCI views CVX as gaining strategic optionality while keeping execution, legal and sovereign-risk haircuts on the production ramp.
items.agciSignal: VENEZUELA SUPPLY OPTIONALITY / MEDIUM-TERM BEARISH OIL OFFSET / EXECUTION RISK

items.headline: New foreign investment in Mexico stalls as USMCA uncertainty delays commitments
items.category: Mexico / USMCA / Nearshoring / Business / Real Estate
items.summary: Reuters reports that new foreign investment commitments in Mexico have stalled as companies delay projects while waiting for greater clarity on the USMCA review and future North American trade rules.
items.whyItMatters: Nearshoring remains structurally attractive but can no longer be underwritten as an automatic capex wave. AGCI raises the weight on signed leases, committed capex, customer credit quality and location-specific infrastructure before assigning value to industrial real estate or supplier expansion.
items.agciSignal: USMCA UNCERTAINTY / VERIFY COMMITTED CAPEX / PENALIZE SPECULATIVE NEARSHORING
